## Pivotting

::: {.incremental}
- Often we want long data for charts and wide data for tables and often have to
convert from one to another.
- From human friendly reading across rows to machine friendly reading down columns.
:::

# pivot wider and longer

Moving data from human friendly reading across a table of data to a computer
friendly long table

Let's convert data like this:

```{r}
tibble::tribble(
  ~org, ~period, ~attendances,
  "abd", "jan", 100,
  "abd", "feb", 200,
  "abd", "mar", 300
)
```

to

```{r}
tibble::tribble(
  ~org, ~jan, ~feb, ~mar,
  "abd", 100, 200, 300
)
```

## Prepare the data

Start with filtering our data and selecting only a few columns

```{r}
library(NHSRdatasets)
library(tidyr)

data <- NHSRdatasets::ae_attendances

data_long <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(
    org_code == "RQM",
    type == "1",
    period >= "2018-08-01"
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    org_code, period,
    attendances
  )

data_long
```

## Make it wider

```{r}
data_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = period, 
                     values_from = attendances)

```

## Answer - pivot wider for breaches

```{r}
data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code == 'RQM', 
                type == '1', 
                period >= '2018-08-01') |>
  dplyr::select(org_code, period, breaches) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = period, 
                     values_from = breaches)
```

# Expand with additional columns

```{r}
data_long <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(
    org_code == 'RF4',
    #type == '1',                     # have not removed the type this time
    period >= '2018-08-01'
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(org_code, 
                period, 
                attendances, 
                type) # have included type back in

data_long
```

Pivoting code is the same as before but type is now available as a column, unchanged

```{r}
data_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = period, 
                     values_from = attendances)
```

# Adding more sites

```{r}
data_long <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(
    org_code %in% c('RQM', 'RJ1', 'RF4'),
    # type == '1',                    # have not removed the type
    period >= '2018-08-01'
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(org_code, 
         period, 
         attendances,
         type) # have included type back in

data_long
```

# Pivot multiple sites

```{r}
data_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = period, 
                     values_from = attendances)

```

# Pivot with the breaches column added

A version with breaches 

```{r}
data_long_breaches <- data |>
  dplyr::filter(org_code %in% c('RQM', 'RJ1', 'RF4'), 
                period >= '2018-08-01') |>
  dplyr::select(
    org_code,
    period,
    attendances,
    breaches, # have breaches type back in
    type
  )

data_long_breaches
```

# Pivot wider with breaches with the same code

Using the same code again but with breaches

```{r}

data_long_breaches |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = period, 
                     values_from = attendances)

```

This doesn't look good - so many NAs

# Pivot wider with breaches but change the code

```{r}
data_long_breaches |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = period, 
                     values_from = c(attendances, breaches)
                     )

```

In this example we now have automatically generated column names prefixed by 
either `attendances` or `breaches`

There are options to change how that is handled, but not going to go into
that now.

# Making wide data long

Using a data frame we created in the last slides

```{r}
data_wide <- data_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = period, 
                     values_from = attendances)

data_wide
```

Make that wide

```{r}
data_wide |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = dplyr::where(is.numeric), # where selects all the numerical columns 
    names_to = 'period',
    values_to = 'attendances'
  )
```
